correctness.rationale: For any real unit sup-norm x, comparability of normalized signed-active faces of x and y forces ∥x−ty∥∞<1 for sufficiently small t>0, so mutual clique patterns form a projective signed-subset antichain. Uniform random sign/permutation flags hit each rank-k pattern with probability [binom(n,k)2^(k−1)]^(−1), proving the LYM inequality and global upper. A fixed-size signed ternary layer attains it. Exact rank-ratio analysis and Stirling at Binomial(n,2/3) mode finish the claim for all n≥1. No complex or infinite-dimensional conclusion. Finite program independently ran 36 layers, 1,274,804 orthogonality pairs, 2 nonternary finite-grid clique searches and all 384 signed flags in dimension four, but proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The exact unrestricted upper bound closes a clear documented gap: the closest full public signed-ternary construction proves only the matching lower bound and explicitly disclaims equality. A signed-active-pattern obstruction and projective signed LYM argument establish the missing all-real-vector bound. The original 2021 upper estimates and 2024 graph recognition theorem do not imply the sharp value. Residual risk: accessible but not complete bibliography, one survey full text unavailable.

value.rationale: The mutual orthograph clique number is an explicitly motivated natural Banach-space invariant in the primary literature. The published strongest known construction supplies an exponentially sharp lower bound but openly lacks an upper bound. Establishing the exact maximum over all real projective directions for every dimension is a substantive complete classification of one scalar invariant; it has nontrivial signed-face and LYM structure, not a narrow arbitrary slice or a renamed lower bound.
